outOfCourt.quote: A ball leaves the court as soon as any part of it would touch a straight edge raised vertically from the boundary. It then becomes a ball in hand and an outside agency.
outOfCourt.source: World Croquet Federation, The Laws of Association Croquet, 7th Edition (February 2021), Law 13.1.1 (with Law 13.1.2 and the Glossary entry 'Boundary'); https://worldcroquet.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/Laws-7th-Edition-master-new.pdf
outOfCourt.note: The boundary is the inner edge of the marking (Glossary: "The innermost edge of the marking or physical line used to define the boundary"; Law 4.3.1). A vertical straight edge on that line is touched by the ball when the ball's outermost point reaches it, i.e. when the centre's distance beyond the line d equals −R. So the ball is off when d ≥ −R: ballRadii = −1, uprightRadii = 0. Law 13.1.2 ("If a determination ... concludes that within the limits of observation the position is on the borderline ..., the decision shall be that the ball is off the court") makes the boundary case count as off, matching the inclusive 'at least'.

hoopRunStart.quote: Subject to the special situations covered in Law 20.4.2 a ball starts to run its hoop in order when it first protrudes out of the jaws of the hoop on the non-playing side when travelling from the playing side to the non-playing side. [...] If a determination of whether a ball at rest, or a ball placed within the jaws of its hoop in order, is in a position to run the hoop to score the hoop point concludes that within the limits of observation the ball is on the borderline between protruding out of the jaws of the hoop on the non-playing side and not doing so, the decision shall be that the ball can run the hoop to score the hoop point from that position.
hoopRunStart.source: World Croquet Federation, The Laws of Association Croquet, 7th Edition (February 2021), Laws 20.1 and 20.6.2 (with Laws 20.4.1, 20.4.2.2 and the Glossary entry 'Jaws of a hoop'); https://worldcroquet.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/Laws-7th-Edition-master-new.pdf
hoopRunStart.note: Glossary: the jaws are "The space enclosed by and including the inner surfaces of the uprights, the surface created by raising a straight edge touching both hoop uprights on the playing side of the hoop from the ground to the crown of the hoop and the equivalent surface on the non-playing side". With cylindrical uprights of radius r whose axes lie in the hoop plane, and d the ball centre's signed distance from that plane (positive towards the non-playing side, i.e. the running direction), the playing-side face is d = −r and the non-playing-side face is d = +r. The ball protrudes out of the jaws on the non-playing side when its leading point passes that face: d + R > r. Law 20.1 says running starts when the ball first protrudes on the non-playing side while travelling forward, so at the start of the stroke it must not already protrude (see also Law 20.4.2.2: "on the playing side of the hoop and does not protrude out of the jaws on the non-playing side at the start of a subsequent stroke"): d + R ≤ r, i.e. d ≤ −R + r. ballRadii = −1, uprightRadii = +1. Law 20.6.2 treats the borderline as able to run, matching the inclusive 'at most'. With R = 0.0460375 m and r = 0.0079375 m the threshold is −0.0381 m. Not captured by a single threshold: Law 20.2.2 lets a ball that started running in an earlier stroke complete it in a later stroke (per-ball state, not position), and Law 20.4.1 bars a ball that first entered from the non-playing side from scoring in that stroke.

hoopRunComplete.quote: Subject to Law 20.2.2, a ball completes running its hoop in order when it ceases to protrude out of the jaws of the hoop on the playing side while travelling forward through the hoop. [...] If a determination of whether a ball at rest has completed running its hoop in accordance with Law 20.2 concludes that within the limits of observation it is on the borderline between protruding out of the jaws of the hoop on the playing side and not doing so, the decision shall be that it has completed the running.
hoopRunComplete.source: World Croquet Federation, The Laws of Association Croquet, 7th Edition (February 2021), Laws 20.2.1 and 20.6.1 (with the Glossary entry 'Jaws of a hoop'); https://worldcroquet.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/Laws-7th-Edition-master-new.pdf
hoopRunComplete.note: Using the jaws geometry in hoopRunStart's note (playing-side face at d = −r), the ball protrudes out of the jaws on the playing side while its trailing point is behind that face: d − R < −r. It ceases to protrude when d − R ≥ −r, i.e. d ≥ R − r. ballRadii = +1, uprightRadii = −1. Law 20.6.1 treats the borderline as completed, matching the inclusive 'at least'. With R = 0.0460375 m and r = 0.0079375 m the threshold is +0.0381 m. Law 20.2.1's reversal clauses (a ball that moves back and rests protruding on the playing side, or exits on the playing side, has not completed) and Law 20.3 (scoring requires completing and then coming to rest not protruding on the playing side, leaving the court, or entering the next hoop's jaws) are expressed against the same threshold.
